title: Check yourself: what the client is really doing

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A settlement service calls QMUX.getMUX("acq-mux") once at startup and reuses that reference for every echo. At 14:10, with Q2 running, an operator edits 20_acq_mux.xml to rename its unhandled queue. What do the service's echoes do after 14:10?

options.text: They come back null after the timeout, since the old object has stopped reading the replies
options.says: Q2 stops the old multiplexer and deploys a new one; the old object's request goes out, but the new one reads the answer and finds nobody waiting

options.text: They come back null after the timeout, since Q2 changed the running object to match the edited file
options.says: Q2 does not change a running object; it undeploys it and deploys a new one, and the new one gets the reply

options.text: They keep getting answers, since Q2 changed the running object to match the edited file
options.says: a changed file makes Q2 undeploy the running component and deploy a new object

options.text: They keep getting answers, since the old object has not stopped reading the replies
options.says: Q2 stops the old object and deploys a new one under the same name; a stopped multiplexer no longer reads the receive queue

origin.section: 1.5.1 Spot the Problem: The Cached Multiplexer

questions.stem: A team's 00_logger.xml has a console SimpleLogListener first, then a ProtectedLogListener with protect set to 2 35, then a RotateLogListener writing log/q2.log. The client sends a purchase for card 5555555555554444. Where does that full card number show up?

options.text: On the console only, since masking applies to the listeners placed after the masking one
options.says: the logger hands the event to its listeners in order, and ProtectedLogListener changes it only for those after it

options.text: On the console only, since masking leaves console listeners alone and covers file listeners
options.says: masking does not depend on the kind of listener, only on its place: listeners after ProtectedLogListener get the masked event

options.text: In the file only, since masking applies to the listeners placed before the masking one
options.says: it is the other way round: listeners after ProtectedLogListener receive the masked event, the ones before it the clear one

options.text: In the file only, since masking covers console listeners and leaves file listeners alone
options.says: masking does not depend on the kind of listener; the console listener before it gets the clear event

origin.section: 1.6 The Log Is Masked Before Anything Writes It

questions.stem: A client's QMUX descriptor was written without a <ready> element. The host is down for an hour of maintenance, so every connection attempt is refused. Before each echo the client checks isConnected(), and it sends the echo with a 20-second timeout. What does each echo attempt look like during that hour?

options.text: It fails at once, since isConnected() reports true but request() checks the link before queueing
options.says: request never checks the link; the message waits in the send queue for up to its timeout

options.text: It fails at once, since isConnected() reports true but the refused link clears the echo from its queue
options.says: nothing removes the echo before its timeout; it waits in the send queue for up to that long

options.text: It fails after 20 seconds, since isConnected() reports true and the echo sits unsent in its queue
options.says: without <ready> a dead link reports connected, so every echo is queued, never sent, and request returns null after the full timeout

options.text: It fails after 20 seconds, since isConnected() reports true and the adaptor takes the echo from its queue to retry
options.says: the echo stays in the send queue until a connection attempt succeeds, and none does; the request's own timeout ends the wait

origin.section: 1.3 `isConnected()` Knows About the Link Only Through `<ready>`

questions.stem: A Spring Boot application starts an embedded Q2 from a SmartLifecycle bean. A new @Service looks the multiplexer up with QMUX.getMUX("acq-mux") in its constructor. What happens when the application starts?

options.text: Startup fails with NotFoundException, since Spring runs the constructor before it starts the bean that runs Q2
options.says: Spring creates every ordinary bean before it starts lifecycle beans, so the constructor runs before Q2 has deployed anything

options.text: Startup fails with NotFoundException, since Q2 deploys the multiplexer only when the first web request arrives
options.says: Q2 deploys every descriptor when it starts, not on demand; the problem is that Q2 has not started yet

options.text: Startup succeeds and the service works, since Spring runs the constructor after it starts the bean that runs Q2
options.says: Spring starts lifecycle beans last, after the services exist

options.text: Startup succeeds and the service works, since getMUX waits in Q2's registry until that name appears
options.says: getMUX is a registry lookup; it throws NotFoundException at once when the name is missing

origin.section: 1.5.2 Spring Starts and Stops Q2, and Nothing Else

concepts: ProtectedLogListener masks the log event only for the listeners listed after it, and never changes the message that is sent.
A Spring application only starts and stops Q2 as a lifecycle bean; services look the multiplexer up when called, because a constructor lookup runs before Q2 has started.
